documents.name: ViaSbrinz: Guttannen–Obergesteln
documents.summary: ViaSbrinz from Guttannen to Obergesteln, Switzerland, is a long historic mule-route crossing of Grimsel Pass through granite and reservoir landscapes.
documents.whyWorthwhile: ViaSbrinz’s Grimsel crossing in Switzerland combines historic mule paths with glacier-shaped granite and large hydropower landscapes.

documents.name: ViaStockalper: Simplon Dorf–Gondo
documents.summary: ViaStockalper in Valais, Switzerland, follows an old mule route from Simplon Dorf through Gondo Gorge to Gondo.
documents.whyWorthwhile: ViaStockalper in Switzerland gives a compact crossing cultural depth through old mule paths, gorge scenery and successive generations of Alpine road engineering.

coverImage.alt: A narrow Stockalperweg path with a wooden railing follows the river in Gondo Gorge.

documents.name: Walenpfad: Brunni–Bannalp
documents.summary: Walenpfad in central Switzerland is a mountainside traverse from Brunni toward Bannalp, with lifts supporting access at both ends.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Walenpfad in Switzerland offers a sustained high mountainside walk whose lift-supported endpoints make a traverse practical.

coverImage.alt: Wildflowers beside the Walenpfad with the mountains above Bannalp beyond.

documents.name: Aussichtspunkt Waid
documents.summary: Waid in Zürich, Switzerland, is a free hillside viewpoint with a broad city, lake and Alpine panorama.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Waid in Zürich gives an easy nearby stop a broad city-and-lake panorama, with Alpine views in suitable weather.

mobility.note: Bus access keeps the required walk short; walking from central Zürich is a longer optional approach.

coverImage.alt: Panoramic view of Zürich from Waid, photographed in 2008.

documents.name: Grossmünster
documents.summary: Grossmünster in Zürich, Switzerland, is a historic church with Romanesque architecture, modern stained glass and an optional tower climb.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Grossmünster in Zürich rewards an old-town visit with historic architecture and distinctive modern stained glass, though restoration limits exterior and tower views.

coreExperience.note: The building is primarily visual and historic.

audio.note: Multilingual audio support is listed for visitor discovery.

mobility.note: The church can be experienced without the tower; Karlsturm requires 187 steep narrow steps and has no lift.

current.note: The church remains visitable during the 2025-2029 restoration, but 2026 scaffolding affects the exterior and portions of the tower panorama.

coverImage.alt: Grossmünster’s twin towers above the Limmat in Zürich, photographed in March 2025.

documents.name: Reichenbach Falls
documents.summary: Reichenbach Falls above Meiringen, Switzerland, combines a high cascade with a historic funicular and a connection to Sherlock Holmes.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Reichenbach Falls in Switzerland combines a characterful waterfall, historic mountain transport and Sherlock Holmes associations, making a rewarding stop in the Hasli valley.

documents.name: Sherlock Holmes Museum Meiringen
documents.summary: The Sherlock Holmes Museum in Meiringen, Switzerland, is a small literary stop centred on a detailed reconstruction of Holmes and Watson’s London sitting room.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Meiringen’s Sherlock Holmes Museum rewards fans with the detail of a reconstructed Baker Street room and the town’s direct connection to the Reichenbach Falls story.

coreExperience.note: The reconstructed room is visual and current visitor evidence reports useful audio interpretation.
Audio interpretation makes the compact experience workable for English-speaking fans.

mobility.note: The museum is small; lower-level access details should be checked for mobility requirements.

legacy-booking-advice.label: Booking advice
legacy-booking-advice.note: Ordinary admission does not require booking. Check seasonal opening before travelling specifically for the museum.

legacy-accessibility-notes.label: Accessibility
legacy-accessibility-notes.note: Small lower-level museum; complete step-free access was not independently verified.

documents.name: St. Beatus Caves
documents.summary: St. Beatus Caves above Lake Thun, Switzerland, have an approximately kilometre-long underground visitor route and a waterfall entrance setting.
documents.whyWorthwhile: St. Beatus Caves in Switzerland combine an underground walk with a striking waterfall entrance, making a worthwhile addition to time around Lake Thun.

coverImage.alt: A walkway and stream emerge through the rocky exit of St. Beatus Caves.

documents.name: Teufelsbrücke, Schöllenen
documents.summary: Devil’s Bridge near Andermatt, Switzerland, is a historic crossing in the narrow Schöllenen gorge on the old Gotthard route.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Devil’s Bridge in Switzerland brings a narrow gorge and historic road engineering together in a compact, atmospheric visit.

legacy-indoor-state.label: Outdoor visit
legacy-indoor-state.note: The short circuit explores the bridge, gorge and historic road structures outdoors.

coverImage.alt: The second and third Devil’s Bridges cross the rocky Schöllenen gorge.

documents.name: Uetliberg Lookout Tower
documents.summary: The Uetliberg lookout tower near Zürich, Switzerland, has 178 steps to a panoramic platform above the mountain’s existing viewpoints.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Uetliberg’s tower in Switzerland raises visitors above nearby obstructions for a wider panorama, making a useful addition to a summit visit.

mobility.note: There is an uphill summit approach from the rail stop and the tower itself has 178 steps.

coverImage.alt: The steel stairs and frame of the Uetliberg observation tower viewed from below.
